* feat(daemon): add the Google Chat platform module

Google Chat needs the daemon half of the four-host platform module: the
relay verifies and forwards events, but replies leave from the daemon over
the Chat REST API, and the daemon must admit each delivery durably before
the relay answers Google.

The module lives in packages/daemon/src/platforms/googlechat/ and touches
core only through registry lines. The connection mints a chat.bot JWT-bearer
token from the service-account key (cached, refreshed before expiry, never
logged), learns the app's users/... identity from members/app or the first
create response, and paces every write through one PlatformSendQueue per
Space, because Google's write quota is per Space and shared by every app in
it. Creates carry a client- id hashed from the durable delivery, the text
block and the segment, plus the same requestId, and reconcile an ambiguous
or conflicting answer by reading that id back rather than allocating a new
one; patches send updateMask=text with markupSyntax beside the text, which
the live probe showed a patch needs to keep Markdown rendering. The
renderer degrades unsupported Markdown readably and the splitter keeps each
message under a 30,000-byte UTF-8 budget, closing and reopening a fence
across a cut. One stream per text block edits the live message at most
every two seconds and lets the final text replace a pending edit; posted
message names land on transcript rows, the daemon's existing record of
what it posted.

The relayIngress strategy requires the durable row and scopes its receipt
by the installed app's transport scope and the Google message identity, so
a redelivery after the turn settled is admitted from the receipt and runs
nothing. With this second implementer, the Linear-specific host port
becomes the shared RelayIngressHost<TConnection>, and Linear moves onto it
without a behavior change. The manifest now marks Google Chat as addressed

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(daemon): keep Google Chat segments under the byte budget and converge replayed messages

Review of the Google Chat daemon module found two correct defects.

The splitter cut once per overflowing line: after a paragraph cut it kept
the remainder and appended the line without re-checking the budget, so a
short paragraph followed by a long one whose last line only fits on its own
produced a 32,001-byte message, over Google's 32,000-byte cap. The cut is
now a loop: after a paragraph cut, a remainder that still overflows with the
line is cut again, closing and reopening a fence or emitting plain text,
until the line fits, with the fence-close reserve accounted for on every
pass. A fence marker too long to ever share a message with a line starts an
empty message instead of looping.

The stream recorded the text it sent as the text on the wire. On a replay
of an admitted delivery the same client id is reused, and Google answers a
repeated messageId or requestId with the original message, whose text the
agent may have changed after a restart; the stream then believed the new
text was showing, skipped the patch, and the transcript recorded text
nobody saw. A segment's text is now whatever Google echoed back, and an
echo that differs, or a response with no text at all, is patched to the
current text in the same reconcile pass, so the wire converges before the
row is written. The connection no longer substitutes the input text for a
missing echo, since that substitution was the very assumption at fault.

fix(daemon): seed Claude's first-start bookkeeping into the private config (#2594)

claude-agent-acp runs `claude auth status --json` at initialize and before
every prompt. With the access token expired, that CLI starts a background
OAuth refresh and exits about 50 ms after opening the connection: the
server has rotated the refresh token, nothing persists it, and the next
process finds a dead token and blanks the shared sign-in. Every daemon
host that ran the probe on a cold private config lost its Claude login
about every eight hours.

The window is the CLI's own first-start bookkeeping: on an empty config
it spends ~100 ms writing firstStartTime, migration flags and the like
before it exits, long enough for the refresh request to leave. Seeded
with those keys, the probe exits ~20 ms after taking the refresh lock,
the timing of a host CLI on its own config, and the request never
leaves. Measured on a daemon host with the token endpoint DNS-blocked:
empty config 59–98 ms, 1 refresh in 5 runs; seeded 16–20 ms, none.

Only the bookkeeping keys travel; sessions, projects, MCP servers and the
account record stay private as before. This narrows the race rather than
closing it, which the design note records.

Step A1 of the Google Chat multi-tenant design (google-chat-integration.md §10):
the message package and relay half.

and sender checks a message gets, and every message, membership and interaction
result carries the event's tenant key (`customers/…` from a Space's customer,

reporting and marking nothing; a bounded per-tenant memo keeps its log line to

`recordTenant` committed the learned key before `syncBot` pushed the spec and

fix(daemon): retry a runtime probe that adopted nothing instead of waiting an hour (#2638)

A pool member is not ready until its runtime probe adopts a table. When the
start-up probe failed (for example, a probe pod that missed its 90 s boot
budget behind a cold pull of a new runtime image), the schedule only tried
again after a full re-probe interval (60 min by default), so a new member
stayed unready past the rollout's progress deadline and the release rolled
back.

an unanswered probe after 30 s, doubling up to the interval, whether or not
the timer is on. A successful probe resets the backoff and returns to the
normal interval.

private runtime HOME let a sandboxed or VM launch refresh the token into its
private copy, which invalidated the host's refresh token; the host kimi then
failed its next refresh and cleared its login. Link the private
.kimi-code/credentials to the host directory (writable to the runtime), as the
Qoder auth directory is, and fold an existing copy-seeded private directory
back into the host, keeping the record with the later expiry and failing

declared credential file beneath it before the credential step could validate
the link. Skip a declared credential destination the shared step excludes,
and exclude every login config.toml names, not only files already on the
host. preparePrivateHome still refuses a link that points anywhere else.

beneath the canonical shared root. Also move the test's redirected link aside
